What to understand at MT9

XP
The in-run currency used for temporary improvements. It is different from permanent Workshop resources.
Era creeping
A community strategy of advancing gradually, earning XP, upgrading divisors and only then moving farther.
/Inf
A divisor display associated with an effectively infinite numerical value. Older routes aim for it; its usefulness and costs depend on current game mechanics.

What you are working toward

  • Work toward the documented Era 1,000 milestone. Check Headquarters for the current collection and total-tier requirements.
  • Improve the affordability of the in-run divisors before relying on rapid Era skipping.

Milestone reference; the current game takes precedence. [S02]

A practical route through this stage

The order below is an suggested route based on community strategies. It is a suggested route, not the only valid build or a tested speedrun.

  1. Develop the research leading to experiments

    Continue Era Workshop progress until the relevant experiment upgrades are available. Focus on reductions affecting the XP price of your in-run divisors. The community references flags older cost targets as obsolete, so compare current prices rather than chasing a number from an old screenshot. [S08] [S01]

  2. Build an XP run that stays alive

    Use a blueprint able to kill enemies steadily without dying or advancing past its own capability. If acceleration jumps too far ahead, temporarily disable the software causing that behavior while you establish the run’s upgrades. This is a controlled farming phase, not a permanent rejection of acceleration. [S08]

  3. Buy both sides of the solution

    Invest in the relevant damage and health divisors rather than assuming one solves everything. Spend XP, advance enough to earn more, and repeat while watching survival. If an elemental power is the actual cause of failure, address its disable as well. [S08]

  4. Use acceleration after the run is prepared

    Once the divisor loop works reliably, enable suitable Era progression software such as Era Surge. Observe the first jump: if the tower immediately fails, return to the setup phase and identify the missing counter or divisor. [S07] [S08]

  5. Choose perks around the limiting resource

    The community references recommends considering International Experts for Town Perk scaling, and Combat Surveillance where XP income is the limiting factor. Read their current effects and compare them with what your run lacks; neither is a substitute for completing the necessary Era research. [S05]

If you are stuck

An old guide says I need exactly 355 XP per upgrade

Do not treat that historical target as a current requirement. Costs have changed; use your game’s actual researched prices.

I survive low Eras but die after enabling all software

Acceleration may be outrunning your upgrades. Build the divisors and disables first, then test progression software in a controlled way.

Ready to move on?

  • Your run can fund its needed divisors before advancing beyond its strength.
  • Era 1,000 and all current promotion objectives are complete.
After the promotion

MT10 adds a special discovery to the Era-depth goal. Reaching a large Era number alone will not necessarily satisfy that discovery. [S02] [S05] [S07]
